title: Impact of Irrigation Eligibility on Crop Revenue

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).
- Rationale: Irrigation eligibility is assigned deterministically by a threshold in the running variable (land slope). Observations just above and below the cutoff are assumed comparable except for eligibility.
- Parameter of interest: The average causal effect of eligibility on crop revenue at the cutoff (local average treatment effect at the threshold).
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of potential outcomes in y varies smoothly with slope at the cutoff; any jump at the cutoff is due to eligibility.
  - No precise manipulation: Farmers cannot precisely sort their land slope around the threshold (validated via density test).
  - Sharp assignment: treated equals the eligibility rule at the cutoff (verified by the jump in treated and low misclassification).
  - SUTVA/local stable composition around the cutoff.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Packages
pkgs <- c("readr", "dplyr", "rdrobust", "sandwich", "lmtest", "rddensity")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(rdrobust)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(rddensity)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s96_data.csv"
df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    running_var = as.numeric(running_var),
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    y = as.numeric(y)
  )

# 2) Cutoff (based on data preview and construction it is 0.5)
cutoff <- 0.5

# 3) Sanity checks of the running variable - treatment rule
df <- df %>% mutate(rule_treated = as.integer(running_var >= cutoff))
misclass_rate <- mean(df$treated != df$rule_treated, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Misclassification rate of eligibility vs. rule 1[ slope >= 0.5 ]:", 
    round(misclass_rate, 4), "\n")

# First-stage jump in treated at cutoff using local linear RD with triangular kernel
# Obtain an optimal bandwidth from rdrobust (we will use it in our own WLS estimator)
get_h_opt <- function(y, x, c) {
  h_opt <- NA_real_
  bw <- tryCatch(rdrobust::rdrobust(y = y, x = x, c = c, p = 1, kernel = "triangular"),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(bw)) {
    if ("h" %in% names(bw)) {
      hv <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(bw$h))
      if (length(hv) >= 1 && all(is.finite(hv))) h_opt <- max(hv, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else if ("bws" %in% names(bw)) {
      hv <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(bw$bws))
      if (length(hv) >= 1 && all(is.finite(hv))) h_opt <- max(hv, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  if (!is.finite(h_opt) || is.na(h_opt) || h_opt <= 0) h_opt <- 0.2
  return(h_opt)
}

# Local polynomial RD estimator via weighted least squares with triangular kernel
rd_local_poly <- function(y, x, c, h, p = 1, donut = 0) {
  dat <- data.frame(y = y, x = x)
  dat$xc <- dat$x - c
  dat$D  <- as.integer(dat$x >= c)
  dat$absxc <- abs(dat$xc)
  use <- which(dat$absxc <= h & dat$absxc > donut)
  dat <- dat[use, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(dat) < 20) {
    return(list(tau = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, ci = c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
                n = nrow(dat), h = h, p = p, donut = donut))
  }
  dat$w <- pmax(0, 1 - dat$absxc / h)
  if (p == 1) {
    fit <- lm(y ~ D + xc + D:xc, weights = w, data = dat)
  } else if (p == 2) {
    dat$xc2 <- dat$xc^2
    fit <- lm(y ~ D + xc + xc2 + D:xc + D:xc2, weights = w, data = dat)
  } else {
    stop("Polynomial order p must be 1 or 2.")
  }
  V <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
  b <- coef(fit)
  seD <- sqrt(diag(V))["D"]
  tau <- unname(b["D"])
  ci <- c(tau - 1.96 * seD, tau + 1.96 * seD)
  return(list(tau = tau, se = seD, ci = ci, n = nrow(dat), h = h, p = p, donut = donut))
}

# 4) Choose bandwidth
h_opt <- get_h_opt(df$y, df$running_var, cutoff)
cat("Baseline bandwidth (h_opt):", round(h_opt, 4), "\n")

# 5) Main RD estimate (local linear, triangular weights)
main_est <- rd_local_poly(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_opt, p = 1, donut = 0)

# 6) First-stage: jump in treated at cutoff
first_stage <- rd_local_poly(y = df$treated, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_opt, p = 1, donut = 0)

# 7) Robustness checks
# 7a) Different bandwidths (half and double)
est_half  <- rd_local_poly(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_opt/2, p = 1, donut = 0)
est_double <- rd_local_poly(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_opt*2, p = 1, donut = 0)

# 7b) Local quadratic
est_quad <- rd_local_poly(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_opt, p = 2, donut = 0)

# 7c) Donut RDD (drop observations extremely close to cutoff)
donut_width <- min(0.05, 0.5 * h_opt)
est_donut <- rd_local_poly(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h_opt, p = 1, donut = donut_width)

# 7d) Placebo cutoff away from true threshold
rng <- range(df$running_var, na.rm = TRUE)
candidate_right <- cutoff + 0.2
candidate_left  <- cutoff - 0.2
placebo_c <- if (candidate_right < (rng[2] - 0.05)) candidate_right else max(rng[1] + 0.05, candidate_left)
h_placebo <- get_h_opt(df$y, df$running_var, placebo_c)
est_placebo <- rd_local_poly(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = placebo_c, h = h_placebo, p = 1, donut = 0)

# 7e) Density (McCrary) test to assess manipulation
dens_obj <- tryCatch(rddensity::rddensity(X = df$running_var, c = cutoff), error = function(e) NULL)
dens_p <- NA_real_
if (!is.null(dens_obj)) {
  s_den <- tryCatch(summary(dens_obj), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(s_den) && "test" %in% names(s_den) && "p_j" %in% names(s_den$test)) {
    dens_p <- as.numeric(s_den$test$p_j)
  }
}

# 8) Print clear numerical results
cat("\n=== Main RD Estimate (Local Linear, Triangular, at cutoff = 0.5) ===\n")
cat("Tau (discontinuity in y):", round(main_est$tau, 4), 
    " | SE:", round(main_est$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(main_est$ci[1], 4), ",", round(main_est$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N used:", main_est$n, " | h:", round(main_est$h, 4), "\n")

cat("\nFirst-stage jump in eligibility (treated) at cutoff:\n")
cat("Delta treated:", round(first_stage$tau, 4),
    " | SE:", round(first_stage$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(first_stage$ci[1], 4), ",", round(first_stage$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N used:", first_stage$n, " | h:", round(first_stage$h, 4), "\n")

cat("\nRobustness checks:\n")
cat("- Half bandwidth: Tau =", round(est_half$tau, 4), 
    " | SE:", round(est_half$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(est_half$ci[1], 4), ",", round(est_half$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N:", est_half$n, " | h:", round(est_half$h, 4), "\n")
cat("- Double bandwidth: Tau =", round(est_double$tau, 4), 
    " | SE:", round(est_double$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(est_double$ci[1], 4), ",", round(est_double$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N:", est_double$n, " | h:", round(est_double$h, 4), "\n")
cat("- Local quadratic (p=2): Tau =", round(est_quad$tau, 4), 
    " | SE:", round(est_quad$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(est_quad$ci[1], 4), ",", round(est_quad$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N:", est_quad$n, " | h:", round(est_quad$h, 4), "\n")
cat("- Donut RD (exclude |x-c| <=", round(donut_width, 4), "): Tau =", round(est_donut$tau, 4), 
    " | SE:", round(est_donut$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(est_donut$ci[1], 4), ",", round(est_donut$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N:", est_donut$n, " | h:", round(est_donut$h, 4), "\n")
cat("- Placebo cutoff at", round(placebo_c, 3), ": Tau =", round(est_placebo$tau, 4), 
    " | SE:", round(est_placebo$se, 4),
    " | 95% CI:[", round(est_placebo$ci[1], 4), ",", round(est_placebo$ci[2], 4), "]",
    " | N:", est_placebo$n, " | h:", round(est_placebo$h, 4), "\n")

if (!is.na(dens_p)) {
  cat("\nMcCrary density test p-value (no manipulation H0):", round(dens_p, 4), "\n")
} else {
  cat("\nMcCrary density test: result unavailable (package/version constraint).\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Eligibility for irrigation should increase crop revenue for farms just above the slope threshold relative to just below it.
- Magnitude: Moderate. Given the scale of y in the preview (roughly centered near zero with values in ±0.4 range), I expect a local effect around 0.10 to 0.25 revenue units at the cutoff.
- Robustness: The effect should be stable across reasonable bandwidth choices, local polynomial orders, and donut exclusions. The placebo cutoff should yield near-zero effects, and the density test should not indicate manipulation. The first-stage jump in eligibility should be close to 1, confirming the sharp design.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare crop revenue for farms just above and below the slope threshold.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligibility for irrigation increases crop revenue.
